sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under conditional unconfoundedness; identification is given and the contribution is limit theory.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with a declared partition into Hall-heavy arms and finite-inverse-moment arms.
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity almost surely; each heavy arm has a uniform second-order Hall lower tail, while each Gaussian arm has a uniformly finite inverse propensity moment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold constrained Bernoulli series likelihood with a boundary exponent profiled against a quasi-uniform spline space.  The schedules retain \(J_N\log N/N\to0\) and additionally impose \(J_N^{-s}\log(N/J_N)\to0\) at \(N=n\) and at every refit size \(N=m\).  Generalized-inverse scales, order-statistic clips, Hill classification, preliminary quantiles, endpoint scores, drift corrections, and densities are all recomputed from the relevant sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 combines Proposition 8.2's deterministic quadratic Knight-remainder and process limit with Proposition 8.3's finite-dimensional infinitely divisible Lévy score limit for the observed true-propensity clipped fixed-quantile estimator.
A growing series-logit propensity fit yields efficient regular-overlap IPW mean estimation.
A nonparametric estimated-propensity QTE estimator is root-\(n\) normal and efficient under regular overlap.
Adaptive scalar \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) resampling yields inference for mean-type effects under irregular identification.
Thresholded cross-fitted AIPW means admit Gaussian inference under tail-amplified nuisance conditions.
Balance-fitted propensities yield regular limit theory for distributional and quantile treatment effects.

body.tldr: A boundary-adapted growing Bernoulli likelihood preserves the compensated infinitely divisible clipped-IPW quantile law under Hall weak overlap.  The signed Riesz expansion gives the rate \(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n\) and derives the amplified transfer condition.  Profiling the redundant boundary direction also proves bounded-arm sample-point consistency under the added approximation-tail condition, which is imposed at both full-sample and refitted subsample sizes.  The resulting procedure has heavy, Gaussian, joint unequal-tail, and conditionally valid arm-vector subsampling laws; the critical fold-labelled Poisson question remains separate.

project_justification.gap: The closest weak-overlap QTE theorem uses the observed true propensity.  Regular estimated-propensity quantile and series-logit results do not supply the singular Hall-boundary signed-functional expansion, empirical clipping correction, or mixed-rate arm recombination proved here.
project_justification.niche: A feasible full-population QTE estimator needs a likelihood expansion that preserves signed cancellation at a Hall boundary, a positive-weight convex argmin, a consistently estimated clipping drift, and shared first-stage covariance.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the constrained-sieve log and signed-functional rates, proves the amplified oracle-transfer condition and its escape-perturbation necessity, establishes profiled bounded-arm sample-point consistency without raw coefficient sup convergence, derives heavy and Gaussian arm laws, recombines unequal arm scales, and validates fully refitted arm-vector subsampling.

body.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky (2025, arXiv:2506.18215v1) provide the observed true-propensity fixed-quantile benchmark but no feasible propensity-estimation theorem.  Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003) motivate regular growing-likelihood projection; the proof here adds singular Hall-boundary information geometry and the signed Riesz rate.  Firpo (2007) supplies the regular QTE context, while the present Gaussian branch permits finite inverse moments and retains shared first-stage covariance.  Heiler and Kazak (2021) motivate irregular subsampling, whereas the proved procedure refits two convex arm estimators and recombines them at full-sample arm scales.  These are positioning comparisons, not claims that the cited papers contain the new expansions.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The theory remains separated from the exact boundary \(\gamma_a=2\), uses a fixed finite quantile set, and obtains uniform likelihood constants on the boundary-smooth subclass rather than the unrestricted Hall class.  The extra approximation-tail condition is required only for the profiled boundary approximation and is imposed after every subsample refit.  The endpoint restriction controls the finite nested score vector, not the full conditional outcome law.  The critical fold-labelled point-process law is not asserted here.
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution is the feasible transfer and inference theory: the constrained likelihood yields its explicit signed-functional rate and corrected amplified condition; the positive-weight argmin has a compensated heavy-arm law; the finite-variance branch has the displayed learned-propensity influence function; armwise recombination covers equal, unequal, and mixed regimes; and complete refitted arm-vector subsampling gives pointwise coverage for each reported quantile.  The bounded mixed control calculation explicitly profiles \(\log(1-x)\), derives sample-point consistency, fixed-rank clipping, divergent Hill classification, and zero drift.  Coverage is pointwise with simultaneous convergence of finitely many coordinatewise errors, not a simultaneous confidence band.  The critical fold-law OEQ remains open outside this unit.
